```{r}
clean <- read.csv("data/processed/penguins_clean.csv")

# Demo: change "Gentoo" to "Adelie" or "Chinstrap", then render again!
chosen_species <- "Gentoo"
species_data <- subset(clean, species == chosen_species)
by_sex <- aggregate(body_mass ~ sex, data = species_data, FUN = mean)
```

## Data

After removing incomplete rows, there are `{r} nrow(clean)` penguins in the dataset across all three islands. Here we focus on the `{r} nrow(species_data)` **`{r} chosen_species`** penguins.

## Results for `{r} chosen_species` penguins

The mean body mass of `{r} chosen_species` penguins was `{r} round(mean(species_data$body_mass))` g. On average, males were `{r} round(diff(by_sex$body_mass))` g heavier than females (@tbl-sex and @fig-mass).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sex
#| tbl-cap: "Mean body mass by sex"
knitr::kable(by_sex, col.names = c("Sex", "Mean body mass (g)"), digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body mass by sex"
#| fig-alt: "Boxplot comparing female and male penguin body mass"
boxplot(body_mass ~ sex, data = species_data, xlab = "Sex", ylab = "Body mass (g)")
```
